newsitem.title: UK: Enron plans $117 mln loan for Polish power station.
newsitem.headline: Enron plans $117 mln loan for Polish power station.

text.p: U.S. power giant Enron International has mandated Bank of America to underwrite a $117 million loan to finance a new power station in Poland, Bank of America said on Thursday.

The 17-year project financing will be used by Enron subsidiary Nowa Sarzyna Cogeneration Company to finance the construction of a station near Nowa Sarzyna in south eastern Poland, the statement said.

The deal is the first non-recourse international project financing in central and eastern Europe to be structured without the involvement of export credit or multilateral agencies, Bank of America said.

The 116 megawatt electric and 70 megawatt thermal gas-fired combined heat and power station will supply PSE, the state-owned Polish power grid company, Organika, a state-owned chemical company, and the city of Nowa Sarzyna.
Completion of the plant is expected in the spring of 1999, the statement said.
